findings.measured: Almost no content above 16 kHz; check whether an MP3/AAC or low-passed file was used as a source.

steps.text: Check the session for MP3 or AAC files, such as samples or imported references.
Look for a low-pass filter on the master or a bus cutting everything above 16 kHz.

findings.measured: Contrast is 1.8 LU; typical for Trap / hip-hop is 2.5 to 7 LU.

steps.text: Press A for automation mode and draw volume so verses sit 2–3 dB below choruses.

other_options.text: Ease the mix-bus compressor: raise the threshold or slow the attack so transients get through.

notes.headline: This mix is technically clean and ready to hand off — the only things worth a look are a missing top octave and how flat the dynamics sit across the song.
notes.summary: Nothing here is broken: levels, headroom and stereo behaviour all measure well for a mix going to mastering. Integrated loudness is -17.08 LUFS with true peak at -4.15 dBTP, so there's plenty of room for a mastering engineer to work. Two things are worth checking before you send it: there's almost no content above 16 kHz, which usually means a lossy source file or a low-pass somewhere, and the loudness range is 1.84 LU, flatter than the 2.5 to 7 LU that's typical for trap and hip-hop. Neither costs you points — they're just choices worth making on purpose.

priorities.title: Find out why there's nothing above 16 kHz
priorities.why: A hard stop at 16 kHz normally means an MP3/AAC made it into the session or something is low-passing the master. Mastering can't put back air that was never bounced, so it's worth ruling out before you hand the file over.

priorities.title: Decide whether the flat dynamics are intentional
priorities.why: Contrast is 1.8 LU against 2.5 to 7 LU typical for trap and hip-hop. That can read as steady and hypnotic, or it can flatten the lift into a chorus. If you want more movement, do it now — mastering will tend to reduce it further, not add it.

listen_for: On the best speakers or headphones you have, listen to cymbals, hats and any vocal sibilance — if the top sounds closed off or dull, chase down the 16 kHz issue.
Solo any imported samples or loops and check whether they sound thinner up top than your recorded or synth material.
Play the transition from verse into chorus and ask whether the chorus actually lifts, or whether it just arrives.
After any volume automation, check on a phone speaker that verses don't disappear when the song gets quieter.
strengths: True peak sits at -4.15 dBTP with 12.9 dB of peak-to-loudness, which is exactly the headroom a mastering engineer wants.
Stereo behaviour is solid: correlation at 0.648, low end at 0.975 and only 0.92 dB lost in mono, so the low end stays put on club and phone playback.
Left/right balance is -0.4 dB — effectively centred, no lopsided imaging to correct.

judge.priority_order: Both findings are info-severity, and the notes put F1 (loss of top-end content, a permanent bounce issue) ahead of F2 (dynamic contrast, which can still be adjusted at mastering), a defensible ordering by audible consequence.
judge.explains_impact: F1 explains that mastering can't restore missing air and ties it to a possible lossy source, and F2 explains that flat contrast can 'flatten the lift into a chorus,' both going beyond raw numbers.
judge.groups_causes: The two findings (air loss and dynamic contrast) are unrelated and are correctly kept as separate priorities rather than being merged.
judge.specific: Notes cite actual numbers (-17.08 LUFS, -4.15 dBTP, 1.84 LU, 0.975 low-end correlation) and reference the Trap/hip-hop style and mix stage directly from the report.
judge.stage_appropriate: The notes frame loudness/headroom purely as room for mastering ('plenty of room for a mastering engineer to work') and explicitly say the info items 'cost you no points,' consistent with a mix-stage report.
judge.faithful: All cited measurements (LUFS, dBTP, LU, correlation, mono loss, balance) match the report, and no problems or causes are invented beyond what's stated.
judge.concise: Given a report with two info-level findings and three strengths, the note length is proportionate, though the four-item 'listen_for' list borders on padding without adding new information beyond the two priorities.
